sanskrit: trīṇi tejāṃsi nocchiṣṭa udīkṣeta kadā cana sūryācandramasau caiva nakṣatrāṇi ca sarvaśaḥ
english: One who is ritually unclean should never gaze upon the three luminaries: the sun and moon, and the stars in all their host.

sanskrit: ūrdhvaṃ prāṇā hy utkrāmanti yūnaḥ sthavira āyati pratyutthānābhivādābhyāṃ punas tān pratipadyate
english: When an elder draws near, the life-breaths of a young man rise up and would depart; but by standing to greet him and offering salutation, he regains them once more.

sanskrit: abhivādayeta vṛddhāṃś ca āsanaṃ caiva dāpayet kṛtāñjalir upāsīta gacchantaṃ pṛṣṭhato 'nviyāt
english: He should salute his elders and have a seat offered to them; with joined palms he should attend upon them, and when one departs he should follow behind.

sanskrit: na cāsītāsane bhinne bhinnaṃ kāṃsyaṃ ca varjayet naikavastreṇa bhoktavyaṃ na nagnaḥ snātum arhati svaptavyaṃ naiva nagnena na cocchiṣṭo 'pi saṃviśet
english: He should not sit upon a broken seat, and should avoid a cracked bronze vessel; he should not eat clad in a single garment, nor bathe naked, nor sleep naked, nor lie down to rest while still ritually unclean.

sanskrit: ucchiṣṭo na spṛśec chīrṣaṃ sarve prāṇās tadāśrayāḥ keśagrahān prahārāṃś ca śirasy etān vivarjayet
english: While unclean he should not touch his head, for all the vital breaths have their seat there; and he should shun the seizing of the hair and any blows upon the head.

sanskrit: na pāṇibhyām ubhābhyāṃ ca kaṇḍūyej jātu vai śiraḥ na cābhīkṣṇaṃ śiraḥ snāyāt tathāsyāyur na riṣyate
english: He should never scratch his head with both hands at once, nor bathe his head too frequently; thus his lifespan will not be diminished.

sanskrit: śiraḥsnātaś ca tailena nāṅgaṃ kiṃ cid upaspṛśet tilapiṣṭaṃ na cāśnīyāt tathāyur vindate mahat
english: Having bathed his head with oil, he should touch no other limb with it, nor should he eat ground sesame; thus he attains long life.

sanskrit: nādhyāpayet tathocchiṣṭo nādhīyīta kadā cana vāte ca pūtigandhe ca manasāpi na cintayet
english: While unclean he should never teach nor study; and in a foul-smelling wind he should not even rehearse the texts in his mind.

sanskrit: atra gāthā yamodgītāḥ kīrtayanti purāvidaḥ āyur asya nikṛntāmi prajām asyādade tathā
english: On this point those who know the ancient lore recite verses chanted by Yama: 'I cut short the lifespan of such a one, and likewise I take away his offspring—'

sanskrit: ya ucchiṣṭaḥ pravadati svādhyāyaṃ cādhigacchati yaś cānadhyāyakāle 'pi mohād abhyasyati dvijaḥ tasmād yukto 'py anadhyāye nādhīyīta kadā cana
english: '—of the twice-born who, while unclean, recites and pursues his private study, and who through delusion practices it even in a forbidden hour.' Therefore, even when intent upon it, one should never study during a time when study is forbidden.

sanskrit: praty ādityaṃ praty anilaṃ prati gāṃ ca prati dvijān ye mehanti ca panthānaṃ te bhavanti gatāyuṣaḥ
english: Those who pass water facing the sun, facing the wind, toward a cow, toward the twice-born, or upon a pathway—they become bereft of their lifespan.

sanskrit: ubhe mūtrapurīṣe tu divā kuryād udaṅmukhaḥ dakṣiṇābhimukho rātrau tathāsyāyur na riṣyate
english: He should void both urine and excrement facing north by day and facing south by night; thus his lifespan will not be diminished.

sanskrit: trīn kṛśān nāvajānīyād dīrgham āyur jijīviṣuḥ brāhmaṇaṃ kṣatriyaṃ sarpaṃ sarve hy āśīviṣās trayaḥ
english: He who wishes to live long should not slight three lean creatures—the brāhmaṇa, the kṣatriya, and the serpent—for all three are venomous as fanged snakes.

sanskrit: dahaty āśīviṣaḥ kruddho yāvat paśyati cakṣuṣā kṣatriyo 'pi dahet kruddho yāvat spṛśati tejasā
english: The angered fanged serpent burns as far as it can see with its eyes; the kṣatriya too, when angered, burns as far as his ardor can reach.

sanskrit: brāhmaṇas tu kulaṃ hanyād dhyānenāvekṣitena ca tasmād etat trayaṃ yatnād upaseveta paṇḍitaḥ
english: But the brāhmaṇa can destroy a whole lineage by his meditation and his very gaze; therefore the wise should attend these three with care.

sanskrit: guruṇā vairanirbandho na kartavyaḥ kadā cana anumānyaḥ prasādyaś ca guruḥ kruddho yudhiṣṭhira
english: One should never persist in enmity with a teacher; an angered teacher must be appeased and won over, O Yudhiṣṭhira.

sanskrit: samyaṅ mithyāpravṛtte 'pi vartitavyaṃ gurāv iha gurunindā dahaty āyur manuṣyāṇāṃ na saṃśayaḥ
english: Whether a teacher acts rightly or wrongly, one must still conduct oneself dutifully toward him here; the reviling of a teacher burns away men's lifespan—of this there is no doubt.

sanskrit: dūrād āvasathān mūtraṃ dūrāt pādāvasecanam ucchiṣṭotsarjanaṃ caiva dūre kāryaṃ hitaiṣiṇā
english: One who seeks his own welfare should pass water far from his dwelling, wash his feet far off, and likewise discard food-leavings at a distance.

sanskrit: nātikalpaṃ nātisāyaṃ na ca madhyaṃdine sthite nājñātaiḥ saha gaccheta naiko na vṛṣalaiḥ saha
english: Not too early at dawn, nor too late at dusk, nor when the sun stands at noon should one set out—nor in the company of strangers, nor alone, nor in the company of the base.

sanskrit: panthā deyo brāhmaṇāya gobhyo rājabhya eva ca vṛddhāya bhārataptāya garbhiṇyai durbalāya ca
english: The path should be yielded to a brāhmaṇa, to cattle, and to kings, to an elder, to one burdened with a load, to a pregnant woman, and to the weak.

sanskrit: pradakṣiṇaṃ ca kurvīta parijñātān vanaspatīn catuṣpathān prakurvīta sarvān eva pradakṣiṇān
english: He should make reverent circumambulation of well-known sacred trees, and keep all crossroads upon his right as he passes.

sanskrit: madhyaṃdine niśākāle madhyarātre ca sarvadā catuṣpathān na seveta ubhe saṃdhye tathaiva ca
english: At noon, in the time of night, and at midnight—always—he should not frequent crossroads, nor at the two twilights either.

sanskrit: upānahau ca vastraṃ ca dhṛtam anyair na dhārayet brahmacārī ca nityaṃ syāt pādaṃ pādena nākramet
english: He should not wear sandals or a garment that has been worn by others; he should ever remain continent, and should not tread one foot upon the other.

sanskrit: amāvāsyāṃ paurṇamāsyāṃ caturdaśyāṃ ca sarvaśaḥ aṣṭamyāṃ sarvapakṣāṇāṃ brahmacārī sadā bhavet
english: On the new-moon day, the full-moon day, on every fourteenth day, and on the eighth day of both fortnights, he should always remain continent.

sanskrit: vṛthā māṃsaṃ na khādeta pṛṣṭhamāṃsaṃ tathaiva ca ākrośaṃ parivādaṃ ca paiśunyaṃ ca vivarjayet
english: He should not eat meat to no sacred purpose, nor the flesh of the back; and he should shun abuse, slander, and malicious talebearing.

sanskrit: nāruṃtudaḥ syān na nṛśaṃsavādī; na hīnataḥ param abhyādadīta yayāsya vācā para udvijeta; na tāṃ vaded ruśatīṃ pāpalokyām
english: He should not be a wounder of others, nor a speaker of cruel words, nor should he by base means seize what belongs to another; the speech by which another would shudder—that searing, hell-winning speech he should never utter.

sanskrit: vāksāyakā vadanān niṣpatanti; yair āhataḥ śocati rātryahāni parasya nāmarmasu te patanti; tān paṇḍito nāvasṛjet pareṣu
english: The arrows of speech fly forth from the mouth, struck by which a man grieves day and night; they fall upon another's tender places—the wise man should never loose them against others.

sanskrit: rohate sāyakair viddhaṃ vanaṃ paraśunā hatam vācā duruktaṃ bībhatsaṃ na saṃrohati vākkṣatam
english: A forest pierced by arrows grows again, and one felled by the axe; but the foul wound inflicted by an ill-spoken word never heals over.

sanskrit: hīnāṅgān atiriktāṅgān vidyāhīnān vayodhikān rūpadraviṇahīnāṃś ca sattvahīnāṃś ca nākṣipet
english: He should not mock those lacking a limb or bearing one too many, the unlettered, the aged, those bereft of beauty or wealth, or those wanting in spirit.

sanskrit: nāstikyaṃ vedanindāṃ ca devatānāṃ ca kutsanam dveṣastambhābhimānāṃś ca taikṣṇyaṃ ca parivarjayet
english: He should shun disbelief, the reviling of the Vedas, and the disparagement of the gods, as well as hatred, obstinacy, conceit, and harshness.

sanskrit: parasya daṇḍaṃ nodyacchet kroddho nainaṃ nipātayet anyatra putrāc chiṣyād vā śikṣārthaṃ tāḍanaṃ smṛtam
english: He should not raise the rod against another, nor in anger strike him down—save in the case of a son or pupil, for whom chastisement for the sake of instruction is sanctioned.

sanskrit: na brāhmaṇān parivaden nakṣatrāṇi na nirdiśet tithiṃ pakṣasya na brūyāt tathāsyāyur na riṣyate
english: He should not speak ill of brāhmaṇas, nor point out the stars by name, nor declare the lunar day of the fortnight; thus his lifespan will not be diminished.

sanskrit: kṛtvā mūtrapurīṣe tu rathyām ākramya vā punaḥ pādaprakṣālanaṃ kuryāt svādhyāye bhojane tathā
english: After voiding urine or excrement, or again after walking upon a highway, he should wash his feet—and likewise before his private study and before eating.

sanskrit: trīṇi devāḥ pavitrāṇi brāhmaṇānām akalpayan adṛṣṭam adbhir nirṇiktaṃ yac ca vācā praśasyate
english: The gods ordained three things as purifiers for the brāhmaṇas: that which is unseen, that which is cleansed with water, and that which is commended by speech.

sanskrit: saṃyāvaṃ kṛsaraṃ māṃsaṃ śaṣkulī pāyasaṃ tathā ātmārthaṃ na prakartavyaṃ devārthaṃ tu prakalpayet
english: Wheaten cakes, rice mixed with sesame, meat, fried cakes, and milk-rice should not be prepared for one's own sake, but should be made ready for the gods' sake.

sanskrit: nityam agniṃ paricared bhikṣāṃ dadyāc ca nityadā vāgyato dantakāṣṭhaṃ ca nityam eva samācaret na cābhyuditaśāyī syāt prāyaścittī tathā bhavet
english: He should daily tend the sacred fire and daily give alms; restraining his speech, he should regularly use the tooth-stick; and he should not be one who sleeps past sunrise, lest he be made to perform an expiation.

sanskrit: mātāpitaram utthāya pūrvam evābhivādayet ācāryam atha vāpy enaṃ tathāyur vindate mahat
english: On rising he should first salute his mother and father, and then his teacher as well; thus he attains long life.

sanskrit: varjayed dantakāṣṭhāni varjanīyāni nityaśaḥ bhakṣayec chāstradṛṣṭāni parvasv api ca varjayet
english: He should always avoid the tooth-sticks that are forbidden, use those sanctioned by scripture, and avoid them too upon the sacred days.

sanskrit: udaṅmukhaś ca satataṃ śaucaṃ kuryāt samāhitaḥ
english: Facing north and with collected mind, he should always perform his purifications.

sanskrit: akṛtvā devatāpūjāṃ nānyaṃ gacchet kadā cana anyatra tu guruṃ vṛddhaṃ dhārmikaṃ vā vicakṣaṇam
english: Without first performing worship of the gods, he should never go to anyone—save to a teacher, an elder, a righteous man, or one of discernment.

sanskrit: avalokyo na cādarśo malino buddhimattaraiḥ na cājñātāṃ striyaṃ gacched garbhiṇīṃ vā kadā cana
english: Those of greater wisdom should not look into a soiled mirror, nor should one ever resort to an unknown woman or to a pregnant one.

sanskrit: udakśirā na svapeta tathā pratyakśirā na ca prākśirās tu svaped vidvān atha vā dakṣiṇāśirāḥ
english: He should not sleep with his head to the north, nor with his head to the west; the wise man should sleep with his head to the east, or else to the south.

sanskrit: na bhagne nāvadīrṇe vā śayane prasvapeta ca nāntardhāne na saṃyukte na ca tiryak kadā cana
english: He should not sleep upon a bed that is broken or split, nor in a hidden place, nor upon a coupled one, nor ever lying crosswise.

sanskrit: na nagnaḥ karhi cit snāyān na niśāyāṃ kadā cana snātvā ca nāvamṛjyeta gātrāṇi suvicakṣaṇaḥ
english: He should never bathe naked, nor ever bathe by night; and once bathed, the truly discerning man should not wipe down his limbs.

sanskrit: na cānulimped asnātvā snātvā vāso na nirdhunet ārdra eva tu vāsāṃsi nityaṃ seveta mānavaḥ srajaś ca nāvakarṣeta na bahir dhārayeta ca
english: He should not anoint himself before bathing, nor shake out his garment after bathing; a man should always put on his garments while they are still moist; he should not pull off his garlands, nor wear them turned outward.

sanskrit: raktamālyaṃ na dhāryaṃ syāc chuklaṃ dhāryaṃ tu paṇḍitaiḥ varjayitvā tu kamalaṃ tathā kuvalayaṃ vibho
english: A red garland should not be worn; the wise should wear a white one, excepting only the lotus and the blue water-lily, O lord.

sanskrit: raktaṃ śirasi dhāryaṃ tu tathā vāneyam ity api kāñcanī caiva yā mālā na sā duṣyati karhi cit snātasya varṇakaṃ nityam ārdraṃ dadyād viśāṃ pate
english: Yet upon the head a red flower may be worn, and likewise a forest blossom; and a garland of gold is never defiling. To one freshly bathed the unguent should always be applied while moist, O lord of peoples.

sanskrit: viparyayaṃ na kurvīta vāsaso buddhimān naraḥ tathā nānyadhṛtaṃ dhāryaṃ na cāpadaśam eva ca
english: The wise man should not put his garment on inverted, nor wear one already worn by another, nor one whose hem is frayed.

sanskrit: anyad eva bhaved vāsaḥ śayanīye narottama anyad rathyāsu devānām arcāyām anyad eva hi
english: One garment should be worn for sleeping, O best of men, another upon the highways, and yet another for the worship of the gods.

sanskrit: priyaṅgucandanābhyāṃ ca bilvena tagareṇa ca pṛthag evānulimpeta kesareṇa ca buddhimān
english: With priyaṅgu and sandal, with bilva and tagara, and with saffron the wise man should anoint himself, each used separately.

sanskrit: upavāsaṃ ca kurvīta snātaḥ śucir alaṃkṛtaḥ parvakāleṣu sarveṣu brahmacārī sadā bhavet
english: He should observe the fast, bathed, pure, and adorned; and at all the sacred seasons he should ever remain continent.

sanskrit: nālīḍhayā parihataṃ bhakṣayīta kadā cana tathā noddhṛtasārāṇi prekṣatāṃ nāpradāya ca
english: He should never eat what has been touched by something licked, nor foods whose essence has been drawn out, nor eat in the sight of onlookers without first offering a share.

sanskrit: na saṃnikṛṣṭo medhāvī nāśucir na ca satsu ca pratiṣiddhān na dharmeṣu bhakṣān bhuñjīta pṛṣṭhataḥ
english: The wise man should not eat while crowded close to others, nor while unclean, nor in the company of the good, nor partake of foods forbidden by the sacred laws, nor eat behind another's back.

sanskrit: pippalaṃ ca vaṭaṃ caiva śaṇaśākaṃ tathaiva ca udumbaraṃ na khādec ca bhavārthī puruṣottamaḥ
english: The best of men who seeks his own welfare should not eat the fruit of the pippala or the banyan, nor the hemp-greens, nor the udumbara.

sanskrit: ājaṃ gavyaṃ ca yan māṃsaṃ māyūraṃ caiva varjayet varjayec chuṣkamāṃsaṃ ca tathā paryuṣitaṃ ca yat
english: He should avoid the flesh of the goat, of the cow, and of the peacock; and he should avoid dried meat as well as what has grown stale overnight.

sanskrit: na pāṇau lavaṇaṃ vidvān prāśnīyān na ca rātriṣu dadhisaktūn na bhuñjīta vṛthāmāṃsaṃ ca varjayet
english: The learned man should not eat salt from his palm, nor curds with barley-meal by night, and he should avoid meat eaten to no sacred purpose.

sanskrit: vālena tu na bhuñjīta paraśrāddhaṃ tathaiva ca sāyaṃ prātaś ca bhuñjīta nāntarāle samāhitaḥ
english: He should not eat with the hair, nor at another man's funeral feast; the self-controlled man should eat at evening and at morning, but not in the interval between.

sanskrit: vāgyato naikavastraś ca nāsaṃviṣṭaḥ kadā cana bhūmau sadaiva nāśnīyān nānāsīno na śabdavat
english: Restraining his speech, not clad in a single garment, never standing unseated, he should never eat upon the bare ground, nor seated apart, nor while making noise.

sanskrit: toyapūrvaṃ pradāyānnam atithibhyo viśāṃ pate paścād bhuñjīta medhāvī na cāpy anyamanā naraḥ
english: Having first given water and then food to his guests, O lord of peoples, the wise man should eat afterward, and not with his mind elsewhere.

sanskrit: samānam ekapaṅktyāṃ tu bhojyam annaṃ nareśvara viṣaṃ hālāhalaṃ bhuṅkte yo 'pradāya suhṛjjane
english: The food set out in a single row is shared in common, O king of men; but he who eats without first offering to his well-disposed companions swallows the deadly hālāhala poison.

sanskrit: pānīyaṃ pāyasaṃ sarpir dadhisaktumadhūny api nirasya śeṣam eteṣāṃ na pradeyaṃ tu kasya cit
english: Water, milk-rice, clarified butter, curds, barley-meal, and honey—once the remnant of these has been set aside, it should be given to no one.

sanskrit: bhuñjāno manujavyāghra naiva śaṅkāṃ samācaret dadhi cāpy anupānaṃ vai na kartavyaṃ bhavārthinā
english: While eating, O tiger among men, one should harbor no misgivings; and he who seeks his welfare should not take curds as a draught to wash down his food.

sanskrit: ācamya caiva hastena parisrāvya tathodakam aṅguṣṭhaṃ caraṇasyātha dakṣiṇasyāvasecayet
english: Having sipped water and let it flow through his hand, he should then sprinkle water upon the great toe of his right foot.

sanskrit: pāṇiṃ mūrdhni samādhāya spṛṣṭvā cāgniṃ samāhitaḥ jñātiśraiṣṭhyam avāpnoti prayogakuśalo naraḥ
english: Placing his hand upon his head and touching the fire with collected mind, the man skilled in proper observance attains pre-eminence among his kinsmen.

sanskrit: adbhiḥ prāṇān samālabhya nābhiṃ pāṇitalena ca spṛśaṃś caiva pratiṣṭheta na cāpy ārdreṇa pāṇinā
english: Having touched his vital organs with water and his navel with the palm of his hand, he should remain steady, and not so with a wet hand.

sanskrit: aṅguṣṭhasyāntarāle ca brāhmaṃ tīrtham udāhṛtam kaniṣṭhikāyāḥ paścāt tu devatīrtham ihocyate
english: At the base of the thumb the sacred ford of Brahmā is declared to lie; and behind the little finger the ford of the gods is here said to be.

sanskrit: aṅguṣṭhasya ca yan madhyaṃ pradeśinyāś ca bhārata tena pitryāṇi kurvīta spṛṣṭvāpo nyāyatas tathā
english: And with that which lies between the thumb and the forefinger, O descendant of Bharata, having touched water in due form, he should perform the rites for the ancestors.

sanskrit: parāpavādaṃ na brūyān nāpriyaṃ ca kadā cana na manyuḥ kaś cid utpādyaḥ puruṣeṇa bhavārthinā
english: He should never utter slander of another, nor anything unkind; the man who seeks his welfare should rouse no wrath in anyone.

sanskrit: patitais tu kathāṃ necched darśanaṃ cāpi varjayet saṃsargaṃ ca na gaccheta tathāyur vindate mahat
english: He should not wish to converse with the fallen, should shun even the sight of them, and should keep no company with them; thus he attains long life.

sanskrit: na divā maithunaṃ gacchen na kanyāṃ na ca bandhakīm na cāsnātāṃ striyaṃ gacchet tathāyur vindate mahat
english: He should not engage in intercourse by day, nor with a maiden, nor with a harlot, nor approach an unbathed woman; thus he attains long life.

sanskrit: sve sve tīrthe samācamya kārye samupakalpite triḥ pītvāpo dviḥ pramṛjya kṛtaśauco bhaven naraḥ
english: Sipping water each at its proper sacred point, when the rite is duly prepared, drinking water thrice and wiping the lips twice, a man becomes purified.

sanskrit: indriyāṇi sakṛt spṛśya trir abhyukṣya ca mānavaḥ kurvīta pitryaṃ daivaṃ ca vedadṛṣṭena karmaṇā
english: Having touched his organs of sense once and sprinkled himself thrice, a man should perform the rites for the ancestors and the gods by the observances revealed in the Veda.

sanskrit: brāhmaṇārthe ca yac chaucaṃ tac ca me śṛṇu kaurava pravṛttaṃ ca hitaṃ coktvā bhojanādyantayos tathā
english: Hear from me too, O Kaurava, the purification that serves the brāhmaṇa's purpose, the conduct that is wholesome, declared for both the beginning and the end of a meal.

sanskrit: sarvaśauceṣu brāhmeṇa tīrthena samupaspṛśet niṣṭhīvya tu tathā kṣutvā spṛśyāpo hi śucir bhavet
english: In all purifications one should touch with the sacred ford of Brahmā; and after spitting or sneezing, by touching water one becomes pure.

sanskrit: vṛddho jñātis tathā mitraṃ daridro yo bhaved api gṛhe vāsayitavyās te dhanyam āyuṣyam eva ca
english: An aged kinsman, a friend, and one who has become poor—these should be given lodging in the house; that brings fortune and long life.

sanskrit: gṛhe pārāvatā dhanyāḥ śukāś ca sahasārikāḥ gṛheṣv ete na pāpāya tathā vai tailapāyikāḥ
english: Doves in the house bring fortune, and parrots, and mynah birds; these in the home portend no evil, and likewise the small oil-drinking creatures.

sanskrit: uddīpakāś ca gṛdhrāś ca kapotā bhramarās tathā niviśeyur yadā tatra śāntim eva tadācaret
english: But when birds of ill omen, vultures, pigeons, or bees take up their abode there, one should then perform a rite of appeasement.

sanskrit: amaṅgalyāni caitāni tathākrośo mahātmanām mahātmanāṃ ca guhyāni na vaktavyāni karhi cit
english: These are inauspicious, as is the cursing of the great-souled; and the secrets of the great-souled should never be divulged.

sanskrit: agamyāś ca na gaccheta rājapatnīḥ sakhīs tathā vaidyānāṃ bālavṛddhānāṃ bhṛtyānāṃ ca yudhiṣṭhira
english: He should not approach forbidden women—the wives of kings, nor their companions, nor those belonging to physicians, to children, to the aged, or to servants, O Yudhiṣṭhira—

sanskrit: bandhūnāṃ brāhmaṇānāṃ ca tathā śāraṇikasya ca saṃbandhināṃ ca rājendra tathāyur vindate mahat
english: —nor those of kinsmen, of brāhmaṇas, of one who has sought refuge, or of relatives by marriage, O lord of kings; thus he attains long life.
